context_purpose: The main contractor must be able to show that every scaffold worker on site holds a valid, recognised high-place work safety certificate.

norm_violation_today.reason: Photocopying the full ID card (ID number, address, birth date) goes well beyond the certificate-validity fact the site needs.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Inspectors may want an auditable record tying a named worker to a certificate number; a bare validity proof loses that unless a signed proof log is kept.

transmission_check.reason: Occupational safety rules oblige the site to verify qualification, but whether a signed proof log would satisfy inspectors rather than copies is not something I can confirm.

context_purpose: The school wants to limit stadium entry to one registered guest per student pass to prevent overcrowding and strangers.

norm_violation_today.reason: Keeping parent and sibling face photos and contact details in a shared cloud folder and group chat after the event outlasts the gate-check purpose.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Nothing material; a one-entry-per-pass check covers crowd control, though it cannot tell who the person is if a pass is handed to someone else.

transmission_check.reason: The school collects for event safety under its own discretion with no known duty to retain photos, so a pass-only flow is allowed.

context_purpose: The onsen operator wants to confirm a visitor meets the venue's age threshold for its conditional tattoo policy.

norm_violation_today.reason: An ID photo with ID number, address and birth date is collected to answer a single over-age question, and then retained.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Nothing for the age rule; the tattoo itself is still judged on arrival.

transmission_check.reason: No known legal duty requires a leisure venue to keep an ID image, so an age-over claim should be acceptable.

context_purpose: The school gate must release a child only to a person authorised by the guardian, and be able to confirm that authorisation.

norm_violation_today.reason: Photographing the ID card leaves a lasting copy of the national ID number in a phone gallery or binder with no deletion date.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: A bearer proof does not tie the credential to the person standing there, so the guard still needs a face or ID check; an audit trail of who left with the child is also thinner.

transmission_check.reason: Child-safety checks at the gate are the school's own procedure and a delegation token serves the same safeguard.

context_purpose: The facility must hand ashes only to the next of kin entitled to act, and be able to show it did so.

norm_violation_today.reason: Collecting proof of kinship is legitimate, but filing ID copies, register printouts and statements naming other relatives in paper records may exceed what is needed.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Disputes between relatives later may need the underlying documents, and a yes/no on authority hides rank among kin that the counter may have to weigh.

transmission_check.reason: Handling of remains and permits is regulated and I cannot confirm whether the rules require copies to be kept.

context_purpose: The ordering contractor wants assurance that each dispatched day worker's high-work certificate is valid on the job date.

norm_violation_today.reason: The hall forwards full certificate scans and ID cards to every contractor who asks, so many parties accumulate data they only need a validity fact from.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Contractors liable for site accidents and site-entry rules may still need the real identity and a record of who worked, which a pseudonym removes.

transmission_check.reason: Site safety rules oblige verification of qualification, but whether a pseudonymous proof alone satisfies the contractor or site gate is not clear to me.

context_purpose: A buyer at a peer-to-peer handover wants some assurance the seller is trustworthy and will not scam them.

norm_violation_today.reason: Showing ID, LINE ID, phone number and bank screenshots that expose other buyers goes beyond a reputation signal for a stroller sale.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: A clean-record count does not stop scammers who build a cheap record, and the buyer cannot identify the seller for recourse if something goes wrong.

transmission_check.reason: The buyer is a private party with no legal duty to collect anything, so a lesser proof is acceptable to them.

context_purpose: Volunteer admins want to grant posting rights for high-value items only to sellers with a proven reliable sales history.

norm_violation_today.reason: Order screenshots with buyer names and chats, profile links and sometimes an ID photo expose third-party data and far more than a sales-count threshold requires.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Little; a threshold count with no disputes answers the admin's question, though cross-platform double-counting is hard to rule out.

transmission_check.reason: Admins are volunteers under no legal duty, so any adequate proof can replace screenshots.
